name: udp-pingpong
algorithm: two UDP sockets of one thread on 127.0.0.1; n rounds of 32 bytes sent a to b, received, sent back to the source and received; sum = 31 sum + byte 0 of each answer, wrapping (tests/bench-lanes/rt-io2/README.md, the row this one enables).
notes: Enabled by std-net2 from rt-io2's parked row (tests/bench-lanes/rt-io2/pending/udp-pingpong): the Mk column is std.net's public API (net.Bind, Datagram.Send, Datagram.Recv); the C, Rust and Go baselines are rt-io2's, unchanged.

Go: net.UDPConn over the netpoller (WSARecvFrom with IOCP on Windows, epoll on Linux); Rust: std::net::UdpSocket, blocking calls; C: blocking sendto and recvfrom; Zig 0.17: std.Io.net IpAddress.bind (mode dgram), Socket.send and Socket.receive over the default std.Io (both checksums agreed, zig build-exe -O ReleaseFast -mcpu=x86_64_v2, std-net2 session 2). Mk: every call through the task scheduler's poller (IOCP on Windows).
